title: How to Protect Yourself from Bank Impersonation Scams
description: Guidance for recognizing fake bank texts, calls, and emails and verifying account problems safely.
text: Bank impersonation messages often claim that an account is locked, a payment is suspicious, or immediate verification is required. They may use a bank's name while directing the recipient to a lookalike website or asking for a password or verification code. Do not use the link or phone number in an unexpected message. Open the bank's official app, type its website address yourself, or call the number printed on the back of the card.

title: How Fake Employment Scams Target Your Online Job Search
description: Guidance on fake recruiters, remote-job offers, and requests for money or personal information.
text: Fake recruiters may contact job seekers by text or email, impersonate a real company, conduct interviews only through messaging, and offer a position unusually quickly. Some send a fake check and instruct the applicant to buy equipment or send part of the money elsewhere. Do not pay to get a job, deposit an unexpected check, or buy equipment from a required vendor. Verify the opening and recruiter through the company’s official website and independently obtained contact information.

title: How to Identify and Avoid Facebook Marketplace Scams
description: Guidance on fake buyers, fake payments, verification-code requests, and marketplace fraud.
text: Marketplace scammers may use newly created accounts, send fake payment notices, claim they overpaid, ask for a refund, or request a verification code to prove that a seller is real. Keep communication and payment on the marketplace when possible. Do not refund an alleged overpayment until the payment is independently verified, and never share a verification code.

title: How to Protect Yourself Against Online Romance Scams
description: Guidance for recognizing online relationships that gradually lead to requests for money or investments.
text: Romance scammers build trust through frequent messages and emotional attention, but avoid meeting in person. Eventually, they may request money for travel, medical problems, an emergency, or a supposed investment. Do not send money, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or account information to an online love interest you have not verified. Discuss the relationship with someone you trust.

title: How to Protect Yourself Against Toll Road Scam Texts
description: Guidance on texts that impersonate toll-collection systems and demand immediate payment.
text: Toll-road scam texts claim that a small unpaid balance will lead to penalties or legal consequences. The link may lead to a lookalike site that collects card, driver’s-license, or other personal information. Do not use the link in an unexpected toll text. Find the tolling agency’s official website yourself and check any balance through a verified channel.

title: Job Scams
description: Official guidance on fake jobs, fake checks, equipment purchases, and employer impersonation.
text: Job scammers may offer work without a normal interview, ask for financial or identity information early, or send a check for equipment and instruct the applicant to send money back. The check may appear in an account before the bank later discovers that it is fake. Do not deposit a check from an unverified employer or pay for promised work. Confirm the position through the employer’s official website and contact the company directly.

title: Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money
description: Guidance on calls and messages that impersonate relatives and demand urgent, secret payments.
text: Family-emergency scammers may claim that a child or grandchild was arrested, injured, or stranded. They often demand immediate payment and tell the recipient not to contact anyone else. Pause before sending money. Call the relative or another family member using a number you already know. A secret payment request is a major warning sign.

title: Avoiding and Reporting Gift Card Scams
description: Guidance on payment demands involving gift cards and what to do after sharing a card number or PIN.
text: Scammers may pretend to be a business, government agency, employer, friend, or relative and insist that a problem can only be solved with gift cards. Requests for the card number, PIN, or a photo of the back of the card are strong warning signs. Do not purchase or send gift cards as payment. If a card was already shared, contact the gift-card company promptly, keep the card and receipt, and report the fraud.

title: How To Avoid a Government Impersonation Scam
description: Guidance on fake agency calls, texts, threats, and immediate payment demands.
text: Government impersonators may claim to represent the IRS, Social Security Administration, Medicare, law enforcement, or another agency. They may threaten arrest, benefit suspension, or legal action and demand payment or personal information. Do not pay or provide information in response to an unexpected contact. Look up the agency's official .gov website and contact it through a verified channel.

title: Investment and Cryptocurrency Scams
description: Guidance on guaranteed returns, fake trading platforms, and cryptocurrency investment pitches.
text: Investment scammers may promise large or guaranteed profits, claim there is little or no risk, and direct victims to fake websites or apps that display invented account growth. They often pressure people to deposit more money or cryptocurrency. Do not invest based on an unsolicited message. Independently research the company and remember that legitimate investments cannot guarantee profits.

title: Selling Stuff Online? Here’s How to Avoid a Scam
description: Official guidance on fake payments, overpayments, checks, and unsafe online sales.
text: A fake buyer may send a check for more than the sale price, claim the extra amount was accidental, and ask the seller to return the difference. The bank may initially make the funds available even though the check is fake. Do not accept a check for more than the selling price, do not return an overpayment, and verify payments inside the marketplace or payment application before releasing an item.

title: How To Recognize and Avoid Phishing Scams
description: General guidance for recognizing suspicious texts and emails that seek passwords, account details, or money.
text: Phishing messages often impersonate banks, government agencies, delivery services, or familiar companies. Common warning signs include unexpected links, urgent threats, requests for passwords or verification codes, and website addresses that do not match the real organization. Do not click an unexpected link. Contact the organization through its official website, app, statement, or a trusted phone number instead.

title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
description: Guidance on fake virus warnings, remote-access requests, and fraudulent support payments.
text: Tech-support scammers may display a frightening pop-up or call unexpectedly and claim that a computer is infected. They often request remote access, payment, passwords, or financial information. Do not call a number shown in an unexpected pop-up, install remote-access software, or allow a stranger to control the device. Contact the company through its official website.

title: Got a Text About Unpaid Tolls? It’s Probably a Scam
description: Official guidance for checking toll claims without using links in unexpected texts.
text: Scammers send texts claiming that an unpaid toll must be paid immediately. The link may lead to a phishing page that requests payment-card or identity information. Do not click or reply. Contact the state tolling agency using a website or phone number you already know is real, then report and delete the message.

title: USPS Package Tracking Text Scams
description: Official guidance on unexpected delivery texts, unfamiliar links, and reporting USPS-related smishing.
text: Scammers send unexpected messages claiming that a package cannot be delivered, an address must be updated, or a small fee must be paid. These messages often contain an unfamiliar tracking link and request payment or personal information. Do not click the link. Visit USPS.com directly or use the official USPS app. USPS-related smishing can be reported to spam@uspis.gov and forwarded to 7726.
